summary: httpz-requests: Telegram-driven remote shell shipped as Cython-compiled typosquat of httpx/requests
details: The distribution name httpz-requests visually collides with the popular httpx and requests packages, but the package metadata describes it as a 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management' and declares python-telegram-bot>=20.0 as a runtime dependency. The top-level __init__.py exposes start_bot from a bot module, and the wheel ships only Cython-compiled.so files (bot, handlers, core, cli, constants, obfuscate, __main__) with no Python sources, hiding the command-dispatch logic, any hardcoded destinations, and any embedded bot token from inspection. The presence of a dedicated 'obfuscate' compiled module in a purported Telegram wrapper is a deliberate anti-analysis signal. Once start_bot is invoked, Telegram updates drive execution on the installer's host — the canonical remote-shell shape, in which a network party operating the bot controls commands run on machines that installed the package. Author-email is the placeholder 'you@example.com' and Project-URL points at 'github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests', consistent with a hit-and-run typosquat rather than a maintained project.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
